payload.title: Recurring explanations become candidate classifiers
payload.description:
Future work, not to be built yet (Ryan, 2026-10-09). When reviewers keep giving the same explanation, that reason is a question the cyclotron should be asking. Detect recurring explanations and propose them, through the existing LLM optimizer proposal path, as a new classifier or an extra classifier question for a person to approve. Never an automatic change.

Acceptance criteria:
- A proposal names the recurring explanation, the number of reviews that gave it, the window it was measured over, and example review ids; nothing is proposed below a configured minimum count.
- The proposal is offered as either an extra question for an existing classifier or a new classifier in the cyclotron, with the evidence counts for each label.
- A person approves or dismisses it; approval goes through the existing candidate measurement and promotion rules (or definition versions, decision-flywheel-ade3088c, for a new classifier); dismissal is remembered so the same proposal is not repeated without new evidence.
- No classifier, question, rubric or review rate changes without that approval.
- subscribe() reports proposed, approved and dismissed events; status() names an open proposal.
